bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Set To Host 60 MW Solar Project in Gaya With SECI's O&M Tender - Saur Energy
bihar_raw_news.content: News Bihar Set To Host 60 MW Solar Project in Gaya With SECI's O&M Tender Bidder will be responsible for O&M of a 60 MW inter-state transmission system (ISTS)-connected solar project. SECI has sought online bids by November 12 and offline bids by November 16, 2026. Chitrika Grover 01 Oct 2026 06:18 IST Follow Us Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) has issued a 60 MW EPC tender to develop a solar project in Gaya, Bihar. It has sought online bids by November 12 and offline bids by November 16, 2026. Advertisment Under the tender, the bidder will be responsible for the design, engineering, supply, construction, commissioning, and operation and maintenance (O&M) of a 60 MW inter-state transmission system (ISTS)-connected solar project. SECI has sought online bids by November 12 and offline bids by November 16, 2026. Advertisment The solar power plant will have a design life of 25 years, with an operation and maintenance period of five years. The project will be developed at Habibpur, Dariaura and adjacent to the Dobhi-Patna Road. Power generated from the project will be evacuated through a 132 kV bay at the 400 kV/220 kV/132 kV PGCIL substation at Chandauti. Brief Scope of Work The scope of work includes design and engineering; procurement and supply of equipment and materials, excluding PV modules; testing at manufacturers’ works; multilevel inspections; packing and forwarding; supply, receipt, unloading and storage at the site; associated civil works; services; permits and licences; installation and incidentals; insurance at all stages; erection; testing and commissioning of the 60 MW AC solar PV power plant and associated equipment and materials on a turnkey basis. Advertisment The contractor will also be responsible for comprehensive operation and maintenance (O&M) of the project for five years from the completion date of the Operational Takeover Guarantee Test (OTGT). The contractor shall prepare the Detailed Design Basis Report (DBR), PERT Chart, up to at least three levels, and Master Drawing List (MDL). These documents must be submitted to the employer/owner for review and approval before detailed engineering. Advertisment Solar Project SECI Bihar tender O&M Gaya Advertisment Read the Next Article

bihar_raw_news.title: Gandak River Embankments Breach at Two Points in Bihar | Daily Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: September 30, 2026 Bihar floods: Gandak embankments breach in Gopalganj, Saran as heavy discharge strains flood defences Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service Source: PTI Embankments along the Gandak River breached at two locations in Bihar’s Gopalganj and Saran districts on Wednesday as heavy water discharge put increasing pressure on flood-control structures, officials said. In Gopalganj’s Baikunthpur block, a roughly six-metre section of the Bandhauli-Sheetalpur-Faizullahpur Zamindari Bund near Sheetalpur village gave way early Wednesday. Authorities warned that floodwater could enter low-lying areas of Parsauni, Sheetalpur and Pakhan and disrupt road connectivity. In Saran, around eight metres of the right Saran embankment at Haijalpur village in Maker block subsided between Tuesday night and Wednesday morning. A flood-control gate was also damaged, allowing water to spread towards low-lying areas of Haijalpur, Parmanand Chhapra and Naukraha. The situation has been compounded by high water levels in the Gandak and Ganga. Bihar’s Water Resources Department said seepage and piping were being reported at several points along embankments, with teams carrying out round-the-clock flood-fighting operations. The Gandak discharge at Valmikinagar Barrage fell from 1.394 lakh cusecs at 4 am to 1.315 lakh cusecs at 7 am on Wednesday. Kosi discharge at Birpur remained around 1.041 lakh cusecs, while Sone discharge at Indrapuri fell sharply from 1.59 lakh to 1.20 lakh cusecs during the same period. The high Gandak discharge follows heavy rainfall in Nepal’s catchment areas. The Valmikinagar Barrage had recorded a peak discharge of about 5.43 lakh cusecs on Tuesday, with flows remaining above 4 lakh cusecs for an extended period. Fresh update: Bihar’s flood monitoring system showed the Gandak at Dumariaghat in Gopalganj still above the highest flood level on Tuesday night and rising, while the river at Bagaha was falling. Officials have advised residents in vulnerable low-lying areas to remain alert and move to safer locations if required. Earlier, two stretches of the Champaran embankment in Bagaha-1 and Bairia had also been damaged. The continuing high flow has put West Champaran, East Champaran, Gopalganj, Saran, Muzaffarpur and Vaishali on heightened alert. with inputs from PTI 0 Likes 0 Dislikes Bookmark 0 Comments Leave a Comment

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 46 SC rules out total ban on firecrackers, ahead of Diwali; Favours balanced approach
national_raw_news.content: Supreme Court has ruled out a complete ban on firecrackers ahead of Diwali and favoured a balanced approach. A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale indicated it will permit the use of certain firecrackers during Diwali but impose specified time limits, ruling out both a blanket ban and unrestricted bursting of crackers. The apex court stressed the need to strike a balance between religious sentiments and the harmful effects of air pollution. It said a complete ban could hurt the sentiments of people celebrating Diwali, while allowing firecrackers throughout the day will adversely affect the environment and vulnerable groups, including children, the elderly and the sick. The apex court was hearing a long-pending matter concerning restrictions on firecrackers in Delhi-NCR and other northern states during the period of severe air pollution. The bench also indicated that it is inclined to accept a suggestion to permit joint firecrackers, or ‘larri’, subject to conditions. Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati sought time till October 15 to place on record the Central Pollution Control Board’s report on barium-based firecrackers, saying outdoor testing of such crackers is yet to be conducted. The bench granted the time sought and said it will consider the report before deciding which categories of firecrackers can be permitted.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | International 160 Saudi authorities arrest Omani co-pilot for stabbing captain and attempting to crash Flydubai fli...
national_raw_news.content: Saudi authorities have arrested an Omani co-pilot after he stabbed the captain and attempted to crash a Flydubai flight traveling from Dubai to Tel Aviv in Israel. The Omani co-pilot stabbed the captain and caused the aircraft to plunge roughly 17,400 feet in under two minutes yesterday. However, passengers and crew members, including off-duty personnel, breached the cockpit, subdued the attacker, and helped stabilise the plane. The flight was diverted and landed safely at Tabuk Regional Airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz described the event as a severe security incident and a suspected terrorist attack. The Israeli Prime Minister described Captain Smit Machchhar, an Indian national, as a true hero who saved the lives of 174 people on board the Israel-bound flight. Mr Netanyahu said Captain Smit Machchhar displayed extraordinary bravery by fighting back and preventing a mid-air disaster. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that in the face of the gravest danger and despite being seriously injured, Captain Smit Machchhar showed immense courage and an unwavering resolve to protect the lives of others. In a social media post, Mr Modi said his valour helped save hundreds of lives and avert a great tragedy. He said, Captain Smit Machchhar is a HERO, and India is proud of him. The Prime Minister prayed for his speedy recovery, renewed strength and good health. US President Donald Trump also hailed Captain Smit Machchhar as a hero for fighting off a knife attack from the Omani co-pilot, opening the cockpit door and calling for help to foil a bid to crash the aircraft. India’s Embassy in Riyadh and its Consulate General in Jeddah said they are closely monitoring the health of Captain Smit Machchhar. In a statement, the Indian Embassy said Captain Machchhar is currently admitted to a hospital in Tabuk and receiving medical treatment. The embassy said initial reports indicate that his condition is stable. The Indian mission said it is in touch with Captain Machchhar’s family and is extending all possible assistance in coordination with the Saudi authorities.

national_raw_news.title: KVIC Chairman hails Lijjat Papad women artisans, says organisation advances 'Vocal for ...
national_raw_news.content: KVIC Chairman hails Lijjat Papad women artisans, says organisation advances 'Vocal for Local' vision Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर KVIC Chairman hails Lijjat Papad women artisans, says organisation advances 'Vocal for Local' vision ANI | Updated: Oct 01, 2026 06:59 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 1 (ANI): Manoj Goyal, Chairman, Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) under the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), addressed the women artisans of Shri Mahila Griha Udyog Lijjat Papad at an event held on Wednesday at the Sri Shanmukhananda Chandrasekharendra Saraswathi Auditorium in Sion (East), Mumbai. According to the MSME, as the chief guest, the KVIC Chairman applauded the work of the women artisans and highlighted the significant role played by organizations like Lijjat Papad in advancing Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Vocal for Local’ and ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’. Addressing the congregation, Manoj Goyal opined that "the journey of Lijjat Papad, established on 15 March 1959 with just seven women and Rs. 80, was not merely an initiative to make Papads, but a dream of becoming self-reliant, living with dignity and standing on one's own feet. The recognition of Lijjat Papad as a Village Industry by KVIC in 1966 gave fresh momentum to this journey. Today, through its 83 branches across 16 states, more than 45,000 women are associated with Lijjat Papad and are progressing towards self-reliance and economic independence. Over the years, the organisation has diversified its product range. Besides papads, it also manufactures spices, flour, detergent and liquid soaps. Its products have reached more than 30 countries, including the USA, Australia, Japan and South Africa." KVIC Chairman said that the greatest strength of Lijjat Papad is its quality, hard work, and discipline. He said, “Lijjat does not merely make papads; it weaves together dignity, self-confidence, and opportunity.” Goyal said that Lijjat Papad’s achievements have also received national recognition. The organisation was honoured with the Best Village Industry Award in 2003, the Brand Equity Award in 2005 and the Women Development Award in 2017. Several international platforms and media organisations have also showcased Lijjat Papad’s inspiring journey to the world, the ministry said. Highlighting the activities and initiatives of the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), the KVIC Chairman said that nearly 5 lakh artisans across the country are being provided employment, out of which 80% are women working in around 3,000 Khadi institutions. Over the past 12 years, the wages of Khadi artisans have increased by up to 275 per cent. He further stated that the production of the Khadi and Village Industries sector has increased to approximately ₹1.25 lakh crore, while sales have reached ₹1.87 lakh crore. Under the Village Industry Development Scheme, more than 3.23 lakh machines and toolkits have been distributed during the last 12 years. Similarly, under the Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP), around 11 lakh new projects have been established so far, with subsidies exceeding ₹30,000 crore, generating employment opportunities for approximately 1 crore people. national_raw_news.title: Ojha gets 1 more yr as PIB principal DG - MillenniumPost
national_raw_news.content: Ojha gets 1 more yr as PIB principal DG Home > Big Story > Ojha gets 1 more yr as PIB principal DG Big Story Ojha gets 1 more yr as PIB principal DG BY MPost 1 Oct 2026 1:30 AM IST X MPost 1 Oct 2026 1:30 AM IST New Delhi: Senior Indian Information Service (IIS) officer Dhirendra Ojha was on Wednesday re-employed as principal director general of the Press Information Bureau (PIB) till September next year. Ojha, a 1990-batch officer, was appointed to the post in July 2024. The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet has approved his re-employment as principal director general, PIB, on a contract basis for one year beyond his superannuation on September 20, 2026, with effect from October 1, 2026, till September 30, 2027, or until further orders, according to an order issued by the Personnel Ministry. With the latest order, Ojha will continue as principal director general, PIB, the principal spokesperson of the central government, till September next year.
